paper_metadata.title: Long-Term Surgical Outcomes of Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Associated With Low-Grade Brain Tumors

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting (tertiary epilepsy center), and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria. The sample is consecutive, and baseline characteristics are well-documented.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We selected patients who had surgery at the epilepsy surgery program of the Seoul National University Hospital from 1995 to 2006, based on a diagnosis of focal epilepsy with a primary brain tumor in the temporal lobe.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as patients within a specific hospital's epilepsy program with specific diagnostic criteria.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The clinical data of 87 consecutive patients diagnosed with tumor-related TLE were analyzed.
items.reasoning: The use of consecutive patients helps minimize selection bias compared to convenience sampling.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from 1995 to 2006
items.reasoning: The recruitment window is explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Seoul National University Hospital
items.reasoning: The specific institution and location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: A minimum postoperative follow-up of 1 year was required. We excluded patients with an extra-axial tumor or a malignant tumor that corresponded to World Health Organization grade 3 or 4.
items.reasoning: Clear inclusion (follow-up time) and exclusion (tumor grade/type) criteria are listed.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not state how many eligible patients were excluded for reasons other than the criteria (e.g., refusal to participate), though 'consecutive' implies high coverage.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Forty-nine patients were male, and 38 were female. The median age at surgery was 22 years (range, 1-62 years). The median age at seizure onset was 14 years... The mean duration of epilepsy was 66 months.
items.reasoning: Comprehensive baseline data including age, sex, duration, and seizure frequency are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the mean follow-up is long, there is a lack of detail regarding the characteristics of patients lost to follow-up or the exact number of patients who dropped out before the 5-year mark, which is critical for actuarial analysis.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: At the time of last follow-up, 60 (69%) patients were being observed in outpatient clinics, and long-term evaluation of the outcome was possible.
items.reasoning: Only 69% were still in active follow-up at the final analysis, which is below the preferred 80% threshold for low risk.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes are defined using the standard Engel classification and objective MRI for tumor control. Although seizure reporting relies on patient recall (standard in epilepsy), the definitions are clear.

items.evidence_snippet: The status of seizure control was evaluated by chart review and was classified according to Engel's classification.
items.reasoning: Engel's classification is the gold standard for epilepsy surgery outcomes.

items.evidence_snippet: the endpoint was defined as the time when recurrence of a totally removed tumor or progression of a partially resected tumor were noticed on follow-up MRI.
items.reasoning: Tumor control was measured objectively via MRI.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
